claims.claim: RAE-1δ staining on TAMs was completely absent in RAE-1-KO mice, confirming the specificity of the RAE-1δ staining.
claims.source: Importantly, RAE-1δ staining on TAMs was completely absent in RAE-1-KO mice, which contain frameshift mutations in the genes encoding RAE-1δ and RAE-1ε, confirming the specificity of the RAE-1δ staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Splenic macrophages, peritoneal macrophages, and blood monocytes in mice bearing B16 tumors expressed little to no RAE-1δ.
claims.source: In contrast to robust TAM expression of RAE-1δ, splenic macrophages, peritoneal macrophages, and blood monocytes in mice bearing B16 tumors expressed little to no RAE-1δ (Figure 1—figure supplements 1C and 3B,C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplements 1C and 3B,C.

claims.claim: Macrophages within the B16 tumor microenvironment are induced to express the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ.
claims.source: These data indicate that macrophages within the B16 tumor microenvironment are induced to express the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 1.

claims.claim: Expression of RAE-1δ in TAMs within B16 tumors was similar at various stages of tumor growth.
claims.source: Expression of RAE-1δ in TAMs within B16 tumors was similar at various stages of tumor growth (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: RAE-1δ staining was negligible or very low on TAMs in RMA-S tumors.
claims.source: In contrast to the findings with B16 tumors, RAE-1δ staining was negligible or very low on TAMs in similarly sized S.C. tumors generated by injection of the RMA-S T cell lymphoma cell line (5 × 106 cells injected) (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: TAMs in primary KP sarcomas expressed robust RAE-1δ.
claims.source: In the KP sarcoma model driven by lentiviral-Cre activation of oncogenic Kras and deletion of Trp53 (DuPage et al., 2009), TAMs in primary tumors expressed robust RAE-1δ (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: TAMs within primary TRAMP prostate tumors mostly lacked RAE-1δ.
claims.source: In contrast, TAMs within primary TRAMP prostate tumors -- a spontaneous adenocarcinoma model driven by expression of SV40 T antigens (Greenberg et al., 1995) -- mostly lacked RAE-1δ (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Tumor microenvironments are differentially capable of inducing NKG2D ligand expression by macrophages.
claims.source: Thus, tumor microenvironments are differentially capable of inducing NKG2D ligand expression by macrophages.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the differential expression patterns observed across tumor models.

claims.claim: Macrophages cultured in control medium showed little to no RAE-1δ expression.
claims.source: Macrophages cultured in the control medium showed little to no RAE-1δ expression, but culture with B16-conditioned medium led to a robust induction of cell surface RAE-1δ (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Culture with B16-conditioned medium led to a robust induction of cell surface RAE-1δ on macrophages.
claims.source: Macrophages cultured in the control medium showed little to no RAE-1δ expression, but culture with B16-conditioned medium led to a robust induction of cell surface RAE-1δ (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: RAE-1δ was induced by culture medium from a KP sarcoma cell line.
claims.source: RAE-1δ was similarly induced by culture medium from a KP sarcoma cell line (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: A soluble factor(s) produced by B16 tumor cells and KP sarcoma cells is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages ex vivo.
claims.source: These results indicated that a soluble factor(s) produced by B16 tumor cells and KP sarcoma cells is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages ex vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the conditioned medium experiments.

claims.claim: Recombinant CSF-1 was sufficient to induce robust RAE-1δ expression on macrophages.
claims.source: Alone among the cytokines tested, recombinant colony-stimulating factor-1 (CSF-1), also known as macrophage colony-stimulating factor (MCSF), was sufficient to induce robust RAE-1δ expression on macrophages (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Macrophages cultured with recombinant CSF-1 along with blocking antibody against CSF-1R failed to induce RAE-1δ.
claims.source: Macrophages express the CSF-1 receptor (CSF-1R) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), and macrophages cultured with recombinant CSF-1 along with blocking antibody against CSF-1R failed to induce RAE-1δ, establishing that the added cytokine acts through CSF-1R (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Recombinant CSF-1 caused upregulation of transcripts of the Raet1d gene, which encode RAE-1δ.
claims.source: We performed qPCR on reverse-transcribed RNA from CSF-1-stimulated macrophages and found that recombinant CSF-1 caused upregulation of transcripts of the Raet1d gene, which encode RAE-RAE-1δ (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qPCR data in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: As little as 3 ng/ml CSF-1 was sufficient to induce detectable RAE-1δ, with high induction levels seen at 10 ng/ml.
claims.source: Stimulation with graded doses of CSF-1 showed that as little as 3 ng/ml was sufficient to induce detectable RAE-1δ in this system, with high induction levels seen at 10 ng/ml (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Induction of other NKG2D ligands by CSF-1 was negligible.
claims.source: Interestingly, induction of other NKG2D ligands by CSF-1 was negligible (Figure 2E), indicating that CSF-1 upregulates RAE-1δ highly selectively.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: CSF-1 upregulates RAE-1δ highly selectively.
claims.source: Interestingly, induction of other NKG2D ligands by CSF-1 was negligible (Figure 2E), indicating that CSF-1 upregulates RAE-1δ highly selectively.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Macrophages derived from bone marrow cells via 7 days of culture with CSF-1 induced robust RAE-1δ.
claims.source: Consistent with our findings, macrophages derived from bone marrow cells via 7 days of culture with CSF-1 induced robust RAE-1δ, whereas parallel cultures in GM-CSF showed little to no RAE-1δ expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Macrophages cultured in GM-CSF showed little to no RAE-1δ expression.
claims.source: Consistent with our findings, macrophages derived from bone marrow cells via 7 days of culture with CSF-1 induced robust RAE-1δ, whereas parallel cultures in GM-CSF showed little to no RAE-1δ expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: B16 cells secreted substantial CSF-1.
claims.source: As measured by ELISA of cell culture supernatants, B16 cells secreted substantial CSF-1, whereas RMA-S cells did not (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: RMA-S cells did not secrete CSF-1.
claims.source: As measured by ELISA of cell culture supernatants, B16 cells secreted substantial CSF-1, whereas RMA-S cells did not (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: KP sarcoma cell lines produced CSF-1, and much more robustly than did B16 cells.
claims.source: KP sarcoma cell lines also produced CSF-1, and much more robustly than did B16 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The concentrations of intratumoral CSF-1 were much greater in B16 tumors than in RMA-S tumors.
claims.source: We used ELISA to analyze CSF-1 protein levels in tumor microenvironments in vivo from mechanically dissociated S.C. tumors and found the concentrations of intratumoral CSF-1 were much greater in B16 tumors than in RMA-S tumors (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: The level of CSF-1 within B16 tumors was substantially greater than serum CSF-1 levels in naïve or tumor-bearing mice.
claims.source: Furthermore, the level of CSF-1 within B16 tumors was substantially greater than serum CSF-1 levels in naïve or tumor-bearing mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), consistent with previous reports describing steady-state CSF-1 levels in circulation (Menke et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: CSF-1R blockade completely abrogated macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16-conditioned medium.
claims.source: We found that CSF-1R blockade completely abrogated macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16-conditioned medium (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: RAE-1δ induction by KP cell line-conditioned medium was completely prevented by antibody blockade of CSF-1R.
claims.source: RAE-1δ induction by KP cell line-conditioned medium was also completely prevented by antibody blockade of CSF-1R (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: CSF-1 is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages.
claims.source: Collectively, these data indicated that CSF-1 is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages, and that CSF-1 is necessary for macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16 and KP tumor cell supernatants in vitro.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claims.claim: CSF-1 is necessary for macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16 and KP tumor cell supernatants in vitro.
claims.source: Collectively, these data indicated that CSF-1 is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages, and that CSF-1 is necessary for macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16 and KP tumor cell supernatants in vitro.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claims.claim: Blockade of CSF-1 or CSF-1R led to substantial reductions in RAE-1δ expression by TAMs in B16 tumors.
claims.source: Mice with established B16 tumors were treated with anti-CSF-1 or anti-CSF-1R, and RAE-1δ on TAMs was analyzed 48 hr post-treatment. Blockade of CSF-1 or CSF-1R each led to substantial reductions in RAE-1δ expression by TAMs (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Blockade of CSF-1R for 2 days had no impact on macrophage cell numbers but drastically reduced macrophage RAE-1δ expression in B16 tumors.
claims.source: Blockade of CSF-1R for 2 days had no impact on macrophage cell numbers but drastically reduced macrophage RAE-1δ expression, whereas treatments for 5 days or longer caused a major depletion in TAM numbers, associated with low RAE-1δ levels on the few remaining macrophages (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Treatments with CSF-1R antibody for 5 days or longer caused a major depletion in TAM numbers in B16 tumors.
claims.source: Blockade of CSF-1R for 2 days had no impact on macrophage cell numbers but drastically reduced macrophage RAE-1δ expression, whereas treatments for 5 days or longer caused a major depletion in TAM numbers, associated with low RAE-1δ levels on the few remaining macrophages (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: A 2 day treatment with CSF-1R antibody resulted in a substantial reduction in RAE-1δ on TAMs in primary KP tumors without a significant reduction in TAM numbers.
claims.source: Similar to the findings with B16 tumors, a 2 day treatment with CSF-1R antibody resulted in a substantial reduction in RAE-1δ on TAMs in primary KP tumors without a significant reduction in TAM numbers, generalizing our findings to spontaneous tumors (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Antibody blockade of the CSF-1/CSF-1R axis suppresses RAE-1δ expression by TAMs in B16 S.C. tumors and autochthonous KP sarcomas.
claims.source: Thus, antibody blockade of the CSF-1/CSF-1R axis suppresses RAE-1δ expression by TAMs in B16 S.C. tumors and autochthonous KP sarcomas.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 4.

claims.claim: Csf1-KO B16 tumors showed markedly lower RAE-1δ expression by TAMs compared with control tumors.
claims.source: Compared with control tumors, Csf1-KO B16 tumors showed markedly lower RAE-1δ expression by TAMs (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: A second, independent Csf1-KO B16 clone also showed substantially reduced RAE-1δ expression by TAMs.
claims.source: Mice injected with a second, independent Csf1-KO B16 clone also showed substantially reduced RAE-1δ expression by TAMs (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Csf1-transduction completely reversed the KO phenotype, and restored RAE-1δ expression on TAMs.
claims.source: To control for off-target effects of Cas9, Csf1-KO B16 cells were stably transduced with control empty vector or a Csf1-expression vector, and injected into mice. Csf1-transduction completely reversed the KO phenotype, and restored RAE-1δ expression on TAMs (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: RMA-S cells stably transduced with a CSF-1-expression vector efficiently induced RAE-1δ expression by TAMs.
claims.source: In contrast, RMA-S cells stably transduced with a CSF-1-expression vector efficiently induced RAE-1δ expression by TAMs whereas transduction with empty vector had little or no effect (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Production of CSF-1 by tumor cells in vivo drives RAE-1δ expression on tumor-associated macrophages.
claims.source: Collectively, these data provide decisive evidence that production of CSF-1 by tumor cells in vivo drives RAE-1δ expression on tumor-associated macrophages.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Macrophages showed robust S6 phosphorylation after CSF-1 stimulation.
claims.source: First, we analyzed activation of the PI3K pathway by intracellular flow cytometry for phosphorylated-S6, a known downstream target of PI3K signaling, in peritoneal macrophages stimulated with CSF-1. Indeed, macrophages showed robust S6 phosphorylation after CSF-1 stimulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Specific inhibition of PI3K p110α prevented CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ expression at low inhibitor concentrations.
claims.source: Interestingly, specific inhibition of PI3K p110α with two different chemical inhibitors (PI3Ka2i and PI-103) prevented CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ expression at low inhibitor concentrations, whereas inhibitors of p110 isoforms β, δ, and γ only inhibited RAE-1δ induction at high inhibitor concentrations, likely due to nonspecific inhibition or off-target effects (Figure 6A and B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6A and B.

claims.claim: Inhibitors of p110 isoforms β, δ, and γ only inhibited RAE-1δ induction at high inhibitor concentrations, likely due to nonspecific inhibition or off-target effects.
claims.source: Interestingly, specific inhibition of PI3K p110α with two different chemical inhibitors (PI3Ka2i and PI-103) prevented CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ expression at low inhibitor concentrations, whereas inhibitors of p110 isoforms β, δ, and γ only inhibited RAE-1δ induction at high inhibitor concentrations, likely due to nonspecific inhibition or off-target effects (Figure 6A and B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6A and B, with speculation about the mechanism.

claims.claim: The two PI3K p110α inhibitors also inhibited accumulation of Raet1d mRNA in CSF-1-treated macrophages.
claims.source: The two PI3K p110α inhibitors also inhibited accumulation of Raet1d mRNA in CSF-1-treated macrophages (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qPCR data in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: PI3K p110α activity is required for induction of RAE-1δ gene expression by CSF-1.
claims.source: These results indicate that PI3K p110α activity is required for induction of RAE-1δ gene expression by CSF-1.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Co-culture of NK cells with CSF-1-induced macrophages expressing RAE-1 molecules efficiently downregulated NKG2D from the NK cell surface.
claims.source: Co-culture of NK cells with CSF-1-induced macrophages expressing RAE-1 molecules efficiently downregulated NKG2D from the NK cell surface, whereas co-culture with RAE-1-KO macrophages had little to no effect on NKG2D levels (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: Co-culture with RAE-1-KO macrophages had little to no effect on NKG2D levels on NK cells.
claims.source: Co-culture of NK cells with CSF-1-induced macrophages expressing RAE-1 molecules efficiently downregulated NKG2D from the NK cell surface, whereas co-culture with RAE-1-KO macrophages had little to no effect on NKG2D levels (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: Co-culture with RAE-1δ-expressing B16 cells led to NKG2D downregulation on NK cells.
claims.source: Similarly, co-culture with RAE-1δ-expressing B16 cells led to NKG2D downregulation, whereas parental B16 cells had little to no effect (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ on macrophages is capable of binding and engaging NKG2D, leading to receptor internalization.
claims.source: Thus, CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ on macrophages is capable of binding and engaging NKG2D, leading to receptor internalization.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 7A and B.

claims.claim: NK cells co-cultured with RAE-1δ-expressing macrophages showed an augmented functional response in vitro to anti-NKp46 stimulation compared to NK cells co-cultured with RAE-1-KO macrophages.
claims.source: NK cells co-cultured with RAE-1δ-expressing macrophages showed an augmented functional response in vitro to anti-NKp46 stimulation compared to NK cells co-cultured with RAE-1-KO macrophages (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: NK cells co-cultured with B16-RAE-1δ cells showed augmented functional responses compared with NK cells co-cultured with parental B16 cells.
claims.source: Similarly, NK cells co-cultured with B16-RAE-1δ cells showed augmented functional responses compared with NK cells co-cultured with parental B16 cells (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: Short-term interactions with CSF-1-stimulated macrophages expressing RAE-1δ had the effect of priming NK cells to respond better when stimulated through a distinct activating receptor in vitro.
claims.source: These data indicate that, in this in vitro system, short-term interactions with CSF-1-stimulated macrophages expressing RAE-1δ had the effect of priming NK cells to respond better when stimulated through a distinct activating receptor.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 7C and D.

claims.claim: The frequency of TAMs among CD45+ cells in B16 tumors was similar in WT and RAE-1-KO mice.
claims.source: However, the frequency of TAMs among CD45+ cells in B16 tumors was similar in WT and RAE-1-KO mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: RAE-1δ levels on TAMs were similar in WT and NKG2D-KO mice.
claims.source: To test whether NKG2D-RAE-1δ interactions select against TAMs with high RAE-1δ expression, we analyzed RAE-1δ expression on TAMs in B16 tumors in WT and NKG2D-KO mice. RAE-1δ levels on TAMs were similar in these two genotypes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Tumor cells secrete the cytokine CSF-1, which induces the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ on tumor-associated macrophages via a CSF-1R-PI3Kα-dependent signaling pathway.
claims.source: Here we describe a novel cellular and molecular axis regulating NKG2D ligand expression on tumor-associated macrophages. We find that, in a set of transplant and spontaneous cancer models, tumor cells secrete the cytokine CSF-1, which induces the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ on tumor-associated macrophages via a CSF-1R-PI3Kα-dependent signaling pathway.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion stated in the discussion based on the collective experimental data.

claims.claim: Macrophages and monocytes were the only hematopoietic cells found to express NKG2D ligands in the tumor models studied.
claims.source: The specificity of NKG2D ligand induction on tumor-associated hematopoietic cells was striking. Macrophages and monocytes were the only hematopoietic cells found to express NKG2D ligands, and ligand expression on those cells was completely limited to RAE-1δ.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: Ligand expression on macrophages and monocytes was completely limited to RAE-1δ.
claims.source: The specificity of NKG2D ligand induction on tumor-associated hematopoietic cells was striking. Macrophages and monocytes were the only hematopoietic cells found to express NKG2D ligands, and ligand expression on those cells was completely limited to RAE-1δ.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: Macrophages treated with CSF-1 upregulated RAE-1δ but not other NKG2D ligands.
claims.source: It is notable that macrophages treated with CSF-1 upregulated RAE-1δ but not other NKG2D ligands, matching the specificity of RAE-1δ induction on TAMs.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: Regulation of NKG2D ligands is tightly controlled and highly specific.
claims.source: These data suggest that regulation of NKG2D ligands is tightly controlled and highly specific, which has also been noted in other cellular and molecular contexts.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the observed specificity of RAE-1δ induction.

claims.claim: PI3K p110α is required for macrophage RAE-1δ induction by CSF-1.
claims.source: We show here that PI3K p110α is required for macrophage RAE-1δ by CSF-1.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: A previous study implicated PI3K p110α in NKG2D ligand induction upon in vitro MCMV infection.
claims.source: A previous study also implicated PI3K p110α in NKG2D ligand induction upon in vitro MCMV infection (Tokuyama et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claims.claim: This report is the first to describe CSF-1 as an inducer of NKG2D ligands.
claims.source: To our knowledge, this report is the first to describe CSF-1 as an inducer of NKG2D ligands.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claims.claim: CSF-1, but not other tested cytokines, induced RAE-1δ on macrophages.
claims.source: CSF-1, but not other tested cytokines, induced RAE-1δ on macrophages.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: Stimulation of macrophages through TLRs was found to induce RAE-1 molecules but not H60 family ligands or MULT1.
claims.source: Stimulation of macrophages through TLRs was found to induce RAE-1 molecules but not H60 family ligands or MULT1 (Hamerman et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claims.claim: Tumor-associated myeloid cells and circulating monocytes in glioblastoma patients were found to upregulate the human NKG2D ligands ULBP1 and MICB.
claims.source: Tumor-associated myeloid cells and circulating monocytes in glioblastoma patients were found to upregulate the human NKG2D ligands ULBP1 and MICB (Crane et al., 2014).

results.result: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in B16 melanoma tumors specifically express the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ, but not other NKG2D ligands. This expression is specific to TAMs within the tumor microenvironment and not observed in macrophages from other tissues in tumor-bearing mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C28-C32, and C115 collectively demonstrate RAE-1δ expression on TAMs in B16 tumors through flow cytometry data (Figure 1A-B), with specificity confirmed by RAE-1-KO mice (C30) and absence in non-tumor macrophages (C31). The gating strategy (C115) and multiple independent experiments provide robust support.

results.result: RAE-1δ expression on TAMs varies across different tumor models. Expression is consistent across tumor growth stages in B16 tumors, robust in KP sarcomas, but negligible in RMA-S lymphomas and TRAMP prostate tumors, indicating tumor microenvironment-specific regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C37 are supported by flow cytometry data across multiple tumor models (Figure 1C and supplements). The differential expression patterns across tumor types are clearly demonstrated, though the mechanistic basis for these differences is not explored in these claims.

results.result: A soluble factor produced by B16 and KP tumor cells is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ expression on macrophages ex vivo, as demonstrated by conditioned medium experiments.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C41 are supported by conditioned medium experiments (Figure 2A-B) showing robust RAE-1δ induction. The experimental design with appropriate controls (fresh medium vs. conditioned medium) provides clear evidence for a soluble inducing factor.

results.result: CSF-1 is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ expression on macrophages in a dose-dependent manner (3-10 ng/ml), acting through CSF-1R. CSF-1 specifically upregulates RAE-1δ but not other NKG2D ligands, and induces Raet1d mRNA expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C49, C57, C86, and C91 are strongly supported by multiple lines of evidence: recombinant CSF-1 induces RAE-1δ (Figure 2C), CSF-1R blockade prevents induction (C43), dose-response data (C45), qPCR shows mRNA upregulation (C44), and specificity for RAE-1δ over other ligands (C46-C47). The cytokine screen (Table 1) confirms CSF-1 specificity.

results.result: B16 and KP tumor cells secrete substantial CSF-1, while RMA-S cells do not. Intratumoral CSF-1 concentrations in B16 tumors are significantly higher than in RMA-S tumors and exceed serum CSF-1 levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C54 are supported by ELISA data (Figure 3A-B and supplements) showing differential CSF-1 production by tumor cell lines and elevated intratumoral CSF-1 in B16 tumors. The correlation between CSF-1 production and RAE-1δ induction on TAMs strengthens the mechanistic link.

results.result: CSF-1 is necessary for macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16 and KP tumor cell supernatants in vitro, as demonstrated by complete abrogation of induction upon CSF-1R blockade.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C56 and C58 are supported by antibody blockade experiments (Figure 3C-D) showing complete prevention of RAE-1δ induction by CSF-1R blocking antibody. This establishes necessity of the CSF-1/CSF-1R axis for the observed effect in vitro.

results.result: Short-term (2-day) antibody blockade of CSF-1 or CSF-1R substantially reduces RAE-1δ expression on TAMs in B16 and KP tumors in vivo without affecting macrophage numbers, while longer treatment (5+ days) depletes TAMs.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C63 are supported by in vivo antibody blockade experiments (Figure 4A-B and supplements) with appropriate time-course analysis. The temporal separation of RAE-1δ downregulation (2 days) from TAM depletion (5+ days) is well-documented and strengthens the conclusion that CSF-1 directly regulates RAE-1δ expression.

results.result: Tumor-derived CSF-1 is necessary and sufficient for RAE-1δ expression on TAMs in vivo, as demonstrated by CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of Csf1 in B16 cells (reducing TAM RAE-1δ), rescue by Csf1 re-expression, and gain-of-function in RMA-S cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C68 are strongly supported by genetic manipulation experiments (Figure 5A-D). The use of two independent Csf1-KO clones (C64-C65), rescue experiment (C66), and gain-of-function in RMA-S cells (C67) provide compelling evidence for tumor-derived CSF-1 as the driver of TAM RAE-1δ expression. This represents decisive genetic evidence.

results.result: PI3K p110α activity is required for CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ expression on macrophages. CSF-1 stimulation activates PI3K signaling (S6 phosphorylation), and specific p110α inhibitors prevent RAE-1δ induction at both protein and mRNA levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C73 and C88 are supported by pharmacological inhibitor studies (Figure 6A-C) showing isoform-specific effects of PI3K inhibitors, with p110α inhibitors effective at low concentrations. S6 phosphorylation data (C69) confirms pathway activation. However, C71 acknowledges that high concentrations of other isoform inhibitors also block induction, likely due to off-target effects, which is appropriately noted as speculation.

results.result: CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ on macrophages functionally engages NKG2D on NK cells, leading to receptor internalization, as demonstrated by NKG2D downregulation in co-culture experiments with RAE-1δ-expressing macrophages or B16 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C77 are supported by co-culture experiments (Figure 7A-B) showing NKG2D downregulation with appropriate controls (RAE-1-KO macrophages, parental B16 cells). This demonstrates functional receptor-ligand interaction, though the biological consequence of this interaction in vivo remains unclear.

results.result: Short-term co-culture of NK cells with CSF-1-stimulated RAE-1δ-expressing macrophages or B16-RAE-1δ cells primes NK cells for augmented functional responses to subsequent NKp46 stimulation in vitro.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80 and C105 are supported by in vitro functional assays (Figure 7C-D) showing enhanced NK cell degranulation and IFNγ production after co-culture with RAE-1δ-expressing cells. However, the manuscript acknowledges this in vitro priming effect may not reflect in vivo function, as discussed in claims C107-C112.

results.result: RAE-1δ expression on TAMs does not affect TAM numbers in B16 tumors, and NKG2D does not select against TAMs with high RAE-1δ expression, as shown by similar TAM frequencies and RAE-1δ levels in WT vs. RAE-1-KO or NKG2D-KO mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C82 and C109 are supported by flow cytometry analysis in knockout mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-B). These negative results are important for ruling out certain mechanisms (e.g., NK cell-mediated TAM killing) and are appropriately documented.

results.result: The CSF-1/CSF-1R/PI3Kα signaling pathway represents a novel mechanism for NKG2D ligand expression on tumor-associated macrophages, integrating tumor-derived signals with macrophage immunoregulatory molecule expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C8 and C83 represent the overarching conclusion synthesizing the experimental findings. This is well-supported by the collective data from multiple experimental approaches (conditioned medium, recombinant cytokine, antibody blockade, genetic manipulation, and pharmacological inhibition). The novelty claim is supported by the discussion (C90, C95).

results.result: Background information on NKG2D receptor, its ligands, signaling mechanisms, and regulation in various cellular contexts, establishing the foundation for the current study.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3 and C9-C23 represent established knowledge from the literature, appropriately cited. These provide necessary context but are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: Prior studies have documented NKG2D ligand expression on various immune cells including macrophages, dendritic cells, and tumor-associated cells in different contexts, providing precedent for the current findings.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C27 and C92-C94 summarize relevant prior literature with appropriate citations. These establish that NKG2D ligand expression on non-tumor cells is not unprecedented, but the specific CSF-1-mediated mechanism is novel.

results.result: The specificity of NKG2D ligand induction is striking: only macrophages and monocytes among hematopoietic cells express NKG2D ligands in the studied tumor models, and expression is limited to RAE-1δ, suggesting tight and specific regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C85 and C87 represent interpretive conclusions from the experimental data (particularly Figure 1). The specificity is well-documented, though the molecular basis for this specificity remains to be elucidated.

results.result: CSF-1 signaling and PI3K p110α have been previously implicated in macrophage biology and NKG2D ligand regulation in other contexts, providing mechanistic precedent for the current findings.
results.evaluation: Claims C89, C97, and C103 cite relevant prior literature establishing that the signaling components identified here have precedent in related biological contexts. This strengthens the plausibility of the proposed mechanism.

results.result: This study is the first to identify CSF-1 as an inducer of NKG2D ligands and represents a novel molecular signature linked to NKG2D ligand induction.
results.evaluation: Claims C90 and C95 assert novelty of the findings. This is supported by the literature review in the discussion and the lack of prior reports of CSF-1-mediated NKG2D ligand induction. The novelty claim is appropriately qualified ('to our knowledge').

results.result: RAE-1δ expression does not fit within the classical M1/M2 macrophage polarization paradigm, as classical M1 (IFNγ) and M2 (IL-4) cytokines failed to induce RAE-1δ.
results.evaluation: Claims C96 and C98 are supported by the cytokine screen data (Table 1) and discussion. This negative result is important for contextualizing the findings within macrophage biology, though the M1/M2 paradigm is acknowledged as controversial.

results.result: RAE-1δ induction requires elevated CSF-1 levels beyond those needed for macrophage survival and maintenance, suggesting macrophages may sense elevated CSF-1 as an indicator of local homeostatic disturbance.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C101 are supported by the dose-response data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) and comparison of tumor vs. serum CSF-1 levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B). Claim C102 is appropriately labeled as speculation, representing an interesting hypothesis for future investigation.

results.result: Speculative discussion of potential biological roles and contexts for macrophage RAE-1δ expression, including tumor adaptation, context-dependent NK cell modulation, and effects on macrophage biology or other NKG2D-expressing cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C104, C110-C112, and C114 are explicitly speculative (appropriately labeled in evidence_type). These represent reasonable hypotheses for future investigation but are not supported by data in the current manuscript. They are appropriately presented as speculation in the discussion.

results.result: Prior studies have shown varied effects of RAE-1 expression on myeloid cells and NK cell function, with context-dependent outcomes including both stimulatory effects in vitro and desensitization in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C108 and C113 cite relevant prior literature, including the authors' own recent work (Thompson et al., 2017), showing that RAE-1 effects on NK cells are complex and context-dependent. This provides important context for interpreting the current in vitro functional data.

results.result: Monocytes in B16 tumors are identified by the surface marker profile CD45+CD11b-hiLy6G-negF4/80-lowLy6C-hi.
results.evaluation: Claim C116 describes the gating strategy for monocytes, supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 3A. This is a methodological detail necessary for interpreting the data showing weak RAE-1δ expression on monocytes (C29).
